title: Fix a Shape
description: Draw a rectangle, then fix it instead of redrawing it: select it, nudge it, and undo cleanly. Point-level editing of paths is covered at the end.

bubble.title: Mistakes are fixable
bubble.body: Every deposit can be moved, restyled, point-edited or undone. Nothing you draw is permanent until you export it.

bubble.title: Draw anything
bubble.body: Press I, steer to the opposite corner, and press I again to deposit a rectangle. Any wobble is fine — you are about to fix it.

bubble.title: Deposited
bubble.body: The rectangle is on the canvas.

bubble.title: Select it
bubble.body: Click the rectangle (mouse buttons still select and drag — keys are for drawing). Selecting is what tells the panel and the operations which object you mean.

bubble.title: Nudge it straight
bubble.body: With the rectangle selected, the arrow keys nudge it. Shift makes the step bigger, Alt/Opt smaller. Steer, snap and nudge are how placement gets exact.

bubble.title: Undo is one step per action
bubble.body: Press Cmd/Ctrl+Z to undo the last action and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Z to redo it. Every deposit, move and restyle is a single undo step.

bubble.title: Fix the points themselves
bubble.body: A selected path can be point-edited: its anchors and curve handles can be picked up and moved, points added or deleted, and corners converted to smooth points — see the Keys Reference under Help for the point-edit keys. Redrawing is the last resort, not the first.
